headline: Advance Surf Fishing and Campground Booking Required
reservation: Park entry is generally accessible via daily fees, but specific amenities like the family campground often fill months in advance during summer. High-demand activities, including surf fishing vehicle access and private group tours of Fort Miles Battery 519, require separate permits or timed bookings. Always verify current system changes and seasonal closures at the official Delaware State Parks portal.

days.title: Dunes and Coastal History

stops.name: Fort Miles Historic Area
stops.detail: Tour the World War II coastal defense batteries and climb the restored observation tower for views of the Atlantic.

stops.name: Walking Dunes Trail
stops.detail: Walk through the maritime forest to observe the 'walking' dunes as they migrate across the coastal landscape.

days.driving: Allow 20 minutes for local park roads; conditions vary with summer traffic
days.note: The observation tower stairs are narrow; pace your climb and check seasonal hours.

days.title: Salt Marshes and Cycling
days.start: Suggested: 8:30 AM from the Seaside Nature Center

stops.name: Gordons Pond Trail
stops.detail: Cycle or walk the elevated boardwalk over salt marshes to spot migratory birds and local wildlife.

stops.name: Cape Henlopen Fishing Pier
stops.detail: Observe the Delaware Breakwater East End Light and watch for the Lewes-Cape May ferry crossing the bay.

days.driving: Allow 30 minutes; boardwalk sections require slow speeds for shared use
days.note: Borrow-a-Bike program is first-come, first-served with a two-hour limit.

days.title: Bay Waters and Heritage

stops.name: The Point
stops.detail: Explore the convergence of the Delaware Bay and Atlantic Ocean, noting seasonal closures for bird nesting.

stops.name: Zwaanendael Museum
stops.detail: Visit this Lewes landmark to learn about the region's 17th-century Dutch colonial origins.

days.driving: Allow 45 minutes including the transfer to downtown Lewes
days.note: Check tide charts before beachcombing at The Point to ensure safe passage.

intel.title: Main Beach Capacity
intel.text: The bathhouse parking area fills early on summer weekends; arrive before peak hours to secure a spot. Alternate lots near Fort Miles offer trail access if the main ocean lot is at capacity.

intel.title: Marshland Connectivity
intel.text: Cellular reception is generally stable near Lewes but can become intermittent along the Gordons Pond boardwalk. Download trail maps at the Nature Center before heading into the marshier interior.

intel.title: Lewes Gateway Services
intel.text: Complete all refueling and grocery needs in Lewes or along Route 1 before entering the park gates. There are no fuel stations located within the state park boundaries.

intel.title: Seasonal Bird Closures
intel.text: Portions of the beach at The Point typically close from March through late summer to protect nesting shorebirds. Plan your beach walks around these protected habitats following posted signage.

intel.title: Drive-on Beach Rules
intel.text: Vehicle access to surf fishing beaches requires a specific permit and required safety equipment. Verify the current permit status and vehicle requirements at the park office before attempting to drive on sand.

plan.arrival: Pick up your rental at DOV and head south through Milford to Lewes. Check into your Lewes accommodation before visiting the Seaside Nature Center for park orientation.
plan.vehicle: Standard vehicles are suitable for all paved park roads; 4WD is strictly required only for permitted surf-fishing beach access. Check rental contracts for off-road restrictions.
plan.goldenHour: The Observation Tower offers a panoramic sunset view, though park exit times vary seasonally.
